# Hub / engine / coordinator: current flow digest

<!-- LIVING digest: the current shape of this subsystem. Update it when you change the subsystem. -->
<!-- Generated by tracing the code; verify file:line before relying on a detail. -->
<!-- digest-base: cmd/ze/hub internal/component/engine internal/component/managed -->

## What it is
The protocol-agnostic wiring that boots the daemon and connects everything else: process bootstrap (`cmd/ze/hub`), the `Engine` supervisor that starts/stops/reloads registered `ze.Subsystem`s in order, the `Coordinator` (a protocol-agnostic facade "created by the hub at startup" that lets any reactor register itself and defer work until every plugin has finished starting), and the managed/fleet client that lets an edge instance pull its config from a remote hub. Two different "subsystem" mechanisms coexist in the real code: `ze.Subsystem` + `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` (used today only by L2TP and PPPoE) and the older Coordinator/`ReactorLifecycle` path (used by BGP, loaded as a config-path plugin through the plugin server, not through the Engine). This digest covers bootstrap and coordination; the per-message engine<->plugin wire protocol (5-stage handshake, EventBus, DirectBridge) is `ai/digests/plugin-transport.md`.

## Flow
1. **Entry.** `ze start` (`cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go` `cmdStart`) opens the `database/` store, detects managed mode via `isManaged` (`cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go`), and calls `hub.Run` / `hub.RunWithManagedClient` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) which both call `run()` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`). `run` reads the config bytes and calls `runYANGConfig` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`). There is ONE runtime and ONE parser: every config the YANG schema accepts boots here, whatever its top-level blocks. `zeconfig.ProbeConfigType` (`internal/component/config/probe.go`) survives, but it no longer selects a runtime -- it answers "does this config declare a top-level bgp block" for the config editor, which starts a web-only daemon when the answer is no.
2. **Coordinator creation.** Inside `runYANGConfig`, after config parse/evolution/PKI setup, `coordinator := zePlugin.NewCoordinator(configTree)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) builds the `*plugin.Coordinator` (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`), documented as "Created by the hub at startup" (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`). `coordinator.SetBootstrap(registry.BGPBootstrap{...})` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) stashes config-load state (config path, CLI plugins, chaos flags, store, health/MRT callbacks) the BGP reactor factory reads back later, avoiding an import cycle between the hub and BGP.
3. **Server + Engine construction.** `pm := pluginmgr.NewManager()` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, `internal/component/plugin/manager/manager.go`) implements `ze.PluginManager` (`pkg/ze/plugin.go`). `apiServer, _ := pluginserver.NewServer(serverConfig, coordinator)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) hands the Coordinator to the plugin server as its `plugin.ReactorLifecycle` (`internal/component/plugin/server/server.go`). `apiServer.SetProcessSpawner(pm)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) and `registry.SetEventBus(apiServer)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) make the plugin server double as the `ze.EventBus` (`pkg/ze/eventbus.go`); there is no separate bus. `eng := engine.NewEngine(apiServer, configProvider, pm)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, `internal/component/engine/engine.go`) builds the `ze.Engine` (`pkg/ze/engine.go`) supervisor.
4. **Subsystem registration (Engine-owned, protocol-agnostic).** Anything implementing `ze.Subsystem` (`pkg/ze/subsystem.go`) registers with the Engine before `Start`: L2TP (`eng.RegisterSubsystem(l2tp.NewSubsystem(...))`, `cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, `internal/component/l2tp/subsystem.go`) and PPPoE (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, `internal/component/l2tp/pppoe/subsystem.go`), each gated on its config block being present. `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` (`internal/component/engine/engine.go`) rejects duplicate names and rejects any call after `Start`. BGP is deliberately NOT registered this way; see Invariants.
5. **Engine.Start joins plugins before subsystems.** The hub binds `pm.SetStartupRunner` before `eng.Start(startCtx)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`). The runner starts the plugin server and joins `WaitForStartupComplete`. `Engine.Start` calls `plugins.StartAll`, whose Manager invokes that runner outside its lock and waits for plugin initialization to finish (`internal/component/plugin/manager/startup_runner.go`). Only then does the Engine start registered subsystems in registration order. A subsystem failure stops those already started in reverse order and stops the plugins.
6. **Plugin phases run inside the startup runner.** `apiServer.StartWithContext` launches `runPluginStartup` (`internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go`): config-path plugins first, then explicit plugins, then auto-load by family, event and send type. Each phase uses `pm.SpawnMore` and the five-stage handshake. A declared initializer must return successfully and answer the ordinary `runtime-ready` callback before its tier completes. These phases finish before Engine-owned subsystems start; the hub does not start the plugin server a second time afterward.
7. **BGP registers into the Coordinator during its own config callback.** The BGP plugin's `OnConfigure` handler (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go`) type-asserts the server's reactor to `registry.CoordinatorAccessor` (`internal/component/plugin/registry/interfaces.go`), builds the reactor via the registered factory, and calls `coord.SetReactor(bgpReactor.ReactorLifecycleAdapter())` (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go`, `Coordinator.SetReactor` `internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`), the only reactor the Coordinator's named map holds in practice (`RegisterReactor`, `internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`, is otherwise unused today). It starts the reactor's listeners immediately (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go`) but defers peer/session startup by registering a `coord.OnPostStartup` callback that rebuilds the peers once from the boot config text to place the declared filter insertions, then runs `bgpReactor.StartPeers()`; a refusal from that rebuild is returned, becomes the plugin server's startup error, and the daemon exits with it (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go`, `Coordinator.OnPostStartup` `internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`).
8. **Startup barrier -> deferred peer start.** When `runPluginStartup` finishes all five phases it calls `signalStartupComplete` (`internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go`), which freezes the schema/subsystem/command registries for lock-free dispatch, fans a post-startup callback out to every plugin (`sendPostStartupToAll`, `internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go`), then calls `s.reactor.SignalPluginStartupComplete()` (`internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go`). The Coordinator (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`) forwards to the BGP reactor and invokes its single stored `postStartup` closure (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`), the step-7 hook: peers start only once every plugin phase has finished, protocol-agnostically. An error that closure returns is the startup error, unless an earlier phase already failed. Back in `main.go`, `apiServer.WaitForStartupComplete(startupCtx)` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, `internal/component/plugin/server/startup.go`) blocks until this barrier fires before the `ze.ready.file` is written (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`).
9. **Managed owners and run loop.** `startManagedServer` (`cmd/ze/hub/managed_server.go`) starts a dedicated managed listener for serving blocks with clients. `runYANGConfig` retains it and defers its synchronous `Stop`. A managed start with storage (`RunWithManagedClient`, which takes a builder of the client configuration, never a built one) creates a `managedClientOwner` (`cmd/ze/hub/managed_owner.go`) whether or not the configuration names a hub. The owner builds a client from the configuration of that moment, wires `CommitOver`, and runs `RunManagedClient` (`internal/component/managed/client.go`) on a context of its own; `request fleet disable` and `request fleet enable` stop and start that client through `managed.FleetTarget` (`internal/component/managed/cmd_fleet.go`), which the hub installs and withdraws. The owner cancels and joins the entire runner before the hub returns the store, including callbacks before reload admission, and starts nothing after that. An unmanaged start (`Run`) has no owner and installs no target. `waitLoop` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) blocks on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP or plugin-server exit (`waitForServerDone`, `cmd/ze/hub/main.go`).
10. **Reload: SIGHUP or managed push both drive `doReload`.** A SIGHUP is read by `handleSIGHUPReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, defined `cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go`); a managed config push instead calls `reloadAfterCommit` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) via the `CommitOver` hook wired in `wireManagedCommit` (`cmd/ze/hub/managed.go`), which stages every push through `storage.StageMachineCandidateOver` over the client's check of the version it fetched over. Both funnel into `doReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go`): load the config tree once, `s.ReloadConfig(ctx, newTree)` (plugin-server diff/apply, owned by `plugin-transport.md`), refresh the shared `zeconfig.Provider` root-by-root (`applyLoadedTreeToProvider`, `cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go`), then `eng.Reload(reloadCtx)` (`engine.go`) fans out to every registered `Subsystem.Reload` (`pkg/ze/subsystem.go`). Any failure after the plugin-server step triggers `rollbackReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go`), replaying the prior tree through the plugin server and restoring the ConfigProvider snapshot.
11. **Managed client connection loop.** `RunManagedClient` (`internal/component/managed/client.go`) loops `runConnection` (`client.go`) with `Backoff` (`internal/component/managed/reconnect.go`, reset on successful auth, `client.go`): TLS-dial the hub, auth, `fetchAndProcess` (`client.go`) which calls `Handler.ValidateConfig` (`internal/component/managed/handler.go`) and, on success, the `ClientConfig.CommitOver` closure (the same `reloadAfterCommit` from step 10; a refusal by its `activeCheck`, a local commit during the fetch, fetches once more over that edit through `refetchOverLocalCommit`), then starts a `Heartbeat` (`internal/component/managed/heartbeat.go`, `NewHeartbeat`) and blocks in `notificationLoop` (`client.go`) handling hub-pushed `config-changed`/`ping` RPCs (`handleHubRequest`, `client.go`) until disconnect, heartbeat timeout, or context cancel. After each config it applies, `fetchAndProcess` calls `ClientConfig.adoptEndpoint` (`client.go`), which reads the applied config's hub-level `client` block through `ClientConfig.Endpoint` (`hubClientEndpoint`, `cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go`): changed hub settings end the connection so the loop reconnects with them at once, and a config with no such block ends `RunManagedClient`. On the hub, `ManagedServer.NotifyConfigChanged` (`internal/component/plugin/server/managed_serve.go`) marks a connected client as owed a push in a pending set rather than a queue, so no change is dropped, and `pushConfigChanged` closes the connection of a client that does not accept the push so its reconnection fetches.
12. **Shutdown: plugin server owner first.** Immediately after construction, `runYANGConfig` defers one `stopAPI := sync.OnceFunc(apiServer.Stop)` and uses it at every explicit stop site. Normal shutdown still calls it before `eng.Stop(stopCtx)`, while startup errors cannot bypass the same join. `setupInfraHook` captures this actual API server after construction and registers hook-built SSH with its existing `OnStop` callbacks, before process cleanup. A local constructor gate/seal joins in-flight acquisition; refused resource registration closes it synchronously before releasing the gate, regardless of callback order. `Engine.Stop` still stops registered subsystems in reverse then calls `plugins.StopAll`; engine/config code names no SSH feature.
13. **Deleted: the multi-process Orchestrator.** Until 2026-08-12 a config whose top-level blocks were only `plugin` and `env` reached a SECOND runtime, `runOrchestratorWithData` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) over `internal/component/hub`, which forked each plugin as `ze <name> --child` and parsed the config with its own hand-written parser. That parser accepted only `external`, so `plugin { internal <name> { use <name> } }` passed `ze config validate` and then failed to boot. `PluginManager` had taken over the forking in March 2026 and both runtimes already reached the same `NewHubAcceptor` (`internal/component/plugin/acceptor.go`), so the orchestrator provided nothing the daemon lacked. The package, its parser and the `ConfigTypeHub` route are gone. `ze bgp --child`, the last child-mode entry point, was deleted with it on the same day.

## Key files
| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `internal/component/engine/engine.go` | `Engine`: `RegisterSubsystem`, ordered `Start`/`Stop`/`Reload` over `ze.Subsystem`s |
| `internal/component/managed/client.go` | `RunManagedClient`/`runConnection`: TLS connect, auth, config fetch, heartbeat, notification loop |
| `internal/component/managed/handler.go` | `Handler.ValidateConfig`: decode + caller-supplied validation of hub-pushed config |
| `internal/component/managed/heartbeat.go` | `Heartbeat`: missed-pong liveness timer feeding the reconnect loop |
| `internal/component/managed/reconnect.go` | `Backoff`: exponential reconnect delay with jitter |
| `cmd/ze/hub/main.go` | Real bootstrap entry point: Coordinator + Engine + plugin server wiring, run loop, shutdown |
| `cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go` | `doReload`/`handleSIGHUPReload`: single-tree-snapshot reload with rollback |
| `cmd/ze/hub/managed.go` | `wireManagedCommit`: bridges a managed config push into the same reload path as SIGHUP |
| `cmd/ze/ze_core_start.go` | `ze start` CLI: managed-mode detection, dispatch to `hub.Run`/`hub.RunWithManagedClient` |

## Invariants & gotchas
- **Two coexisting "subsystem" mechanisms.** `ze.Subsystem` + `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` (`pkg/ze/subsystem.go`, `engine.go`) is used today only by L2TP and PPPoE. BGP (and iface/fib/etc.) load as config-path plugins through the plugin server and register into the Coordinator instead (step 7); so despite the older architecture note calling the BGP daemon a subsystem, it does not implement `ze.Subsystem` or call `Engine.RegisterSubsystem` in the current code.
- **Engine.Start joins complete plugin startup.** `Manager.StartAll` invokes the hub-bound runner and waits for its completion before Engine-owned subsystems start. `StopAll` cancels and joins an in-flight runner. The hub must bind the runner before startup (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, `internal/component/plugin/manager/startup_runner.go`).
- **Daemon SSH ownership is not Engine registration.** The BGP factory runs the
  infrastructure hook before its reactor receives params.APIServer. The hook
  therefore captures the already-constructed hub server instead and registers
  actual SSH Stop callbacks on its OnStop lifetime (`cmd/ze/hub/infra_setup.go`).
  All daemon-owned API stops share main's OnceFunc; a second direct Server.Stop
  could otherwise return while the first callback invocation still drains.
  Reactor abort/cleanup stops its API only when !externalServer; production
  CreateReactor(..., false) borrows this hub API server and cannot stop it.
  REST/gRPC/gNMI/web shutdown handles close their own transport servers, not
  this owner. Standalone no-BGP SSH keeps its own existing deferred Stop.
- **`Coordinator.postStartup` is a single closure, not a list** (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`). Only BGP calls `OnPostStartup` today (`internal/component/bgp/plugin/register.go`); a second protocol reactor calling it would silently overwrite BGP's deferred-peer-start hook. `RegisterReactor`'s named-reactor map (`internal/component/plugin/coordinator.go`) is likewise unused beyond the single `"bgp"` entry set by `SetReactor`.
- **One config, one parser, one runtime.** `ProbeConfigType` (`internal/component/config/probe.go`) no longer routes: `run` (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`) calls `runYANGConfig` unconditionally. What `ze config validate` accepts is what boots, and the agreement is held by `test/plugin/config-validate-agrees-with-boot.ci`.
- **Docs describe an aspirational, not-yet-collapsed design.** `docs/architecture/hub-architecture.md` is explicitly headed "Design aspiration (partially implemented)"; `docs/architecture/subsystem-wiring.md` and `docs/architecture/plugin-manager-wiring.md` both describe an intermediate "BGPSubsystem wraps Server" shape that the live code does not have (`Server`/`apiServer` is created directly in `cmd/ze/hub/main.go`, before any reactor exists). Both docs point back at `cmd/ze/hub/main.go` as authoritative; trust the code over the diagrams.
- **The fleet server has its own listener and owner.** `startManagedServer` (`cmd/ze/hub/managed_server.go`) wires `ManagedServer` (`internal/component/plugin/server/managed_serve.go`) to the same store's client configs and write observer. Its synchronous `Stop` joins config-fetch and config-changed reads. The observer only enqueues notifications and cannot read the store after those workers end. Serving clients and an outbound managed connection can coexist.
- **Managed pushes and SIGHUP share one commit path.** `wireManagedCommit`'s `CommitOver` (`cmd/ze/hub/managed.go`) writes a candidate version over the client's check then calls the exact same `reloadAfterCommit` closure SIGHUP/API/SSH commits use (`cmd/ze/hub/main.go`), so a managed push gets the same validate/diff/apply/rollback guarantees as any other commit.
- **Reload rollback covers the plugin server and ConfigProvider, not subsystems individually.** `rollbackReload` (`cmd/ze/hub/main_reload.go`) replays the prior tree through `s.ReloadConfig` and restores the ConfigProvider snapshot, then calls `eng.Reload` again with the restored provider; it does not separately undo whatever partial state a subsystem's own `Reload` mutated before the failure.
